A file must lie under one of the media roots (``EP_MEDIA_ROOTS``); a host path in a

does the same and answers with the recording's sources.)

get.description:
Artists, release groups, recordings, radio shows and radio episodes matching
``q``, best first.

Accent- and case-insensitive; finds prefixes ("bjo" finds "Björk"), tolerates small
typos, and matches artist and title together ("nina simone sinnerman"). ``types``
(repeatable) limits the entity types; default all. ``per_type`` caps the hits of
each type (for results grouped by type), ``limit`` all of them. ``tag_id``: only
entities with that tag. Give ``q``, ``tag_id`` or both: without ``q``, everything
with the tag, by type (artists, release groups, recordings, radio shows, radio
episodes) and then by name, with ``score`` null, in pages (``limit``, ``offset``;
``X-Total-Count`` is the length of the whole list). A search with ``q`` is ranked and
not paged: ``offset`` must be 0 and ``X-Total-Count`` is the number of hits.
Artists and recordings only known from radio tracklists are left out unless
``include_radio_only``.

Radio episodes are also found by what they played: an episode that played a
matching recording, or a track of a matching release group, is a hit with
``radio_match`` (the entry and its time). Release group hits carry their track
count, artist hits their release group and loose recording counts. Each hit
carries the link to write for it (``link``: ``[[type:uuid|Title]]``, the UUID being
the MBID if there is one, else the id).

X-Total-Count.description: Number of items in the whole list (all pages).

get.description:
Find an entity by MBID or internal ID (as used in note links).

A release group is also found by the MBID of its release. Radio shows and episodes
have internal IDs only.

``"a phrase"``, ``or``, ``-word``), best first, with the entity each belongs to and
a snippet. Case- and accent-insensitive, no stemming (notes mix languages); links
count as their display text. ``types`` (repeatable) limits the entity types.

X-Total-Count.description: Number of items in the whole list (all pages).

recording's). An entity without a note has an empty one. Links come with their

show them without further requests.

put.description:

``updated_at`` the edit started from: if the note changed since (and the new body
differs from the current one), nothing is saved and the answer is a 409 with the
current note. Links are parsed and resolved again on every save.

409.description: The note changed since the edit started

get.description: Search MusicBrainz for artists, releases or recordings (``q`` is plain text).

post.description:
Add an artist, a release or a recording from MusicBrainz to the catalogue, as
metadata only (no files, no cover), and return it (with the link to write for it).

An artist or recording with the MBID in the library is returned as it is. A
release becomes a release group with its artists, recordings, tracks and ISRCs; rows
with known MBIDs are reused, and importing the same release again adds only what is
missing (409 if the release group was imported from a different release). A
recording becomes a standalone recording (no track) with its artists and ISRCs.

Queue an import. ``folder``: a directory under the media roots, imported in place.
``bandcamp``: an album or track page; ``youtube``: a video (with chapters: a
single-file album) or a playlist (one release group); ``nts``: an NTS episode page
(the episode with its tracklist matched against the library); downloaded into the
managed library. URLs are stored canonical (tracking parameters dropped).

get.description:
Jobs, newest first. The inbox: ``attention=true`` (``needs_review`` and
``failed`` jobs, waiting for an answer, a retry or a dismiss); the rest of the queue
without them: ``attention=false``. Each with what it imports (title, cover, counts),
its progress, what it is stuck on and the job a queued one waits for.

parameters.name: attention

schema.description: true: only jobs that need attention (``needs_review``, ``failed``: the inbox); false: only the others. Combines with ``state``.
schema.title: Attention

parameters.description: true: only jobs that need attention (``needs_review``, ``failed``: the inbox); false: only the others. Combines with ``state``.

X-Total-Count.description: Number of items in the whole list (all pages).

get.description: State, progress, log and proposal (with its issues) of a job.

post.description:
Answer issues by id, then run the job again with the answers.

Each answer must be one of its issue's ``choices`` (and, for ``pick_candidate``, name
one of its candidates); answered issues can be answered again. ``retry`` clears a
stored answer and simply runs again. 422 for an unknown issue or a choice that does
not fit; 409 unless the job is ``needs_review`` or ``failed``.

Run a ``needs_review``, ``failed`` or ``done`` job again from the start, with its
answers: failed downloads and reads are tried again (``ImportCountsRead.failed``).
A done job creates nothing new: files already imported are left out.

Take a ``needs_review`` or ``failed`` job out of the inbox. Nothing more is
imported, and its downloads are deleted; the watcher does not queue the folder again
until it changes.

Stop a ``queued`` or ``running`` job and take it out of the queue (it becomes
``dismissed``). A running job stops at its next step (a running download is
killed); what it fetched is deleted and nothing is imported. A job already writing
to the library (``applying``) finishes: 409.

get.description:
The audio file of an incoming track (``IncomingTrack.key``), to preview it in

get.description:

canonical form. All fields null for a URL EP does not know.

when they last queued an import.

post.description:

see ``scan_watch_dir``.

patch.description:
Enable or disable watching. The baseline stays: folders that changed while the
directory was disabled are imported once it is enabled again.

delete.description: Stop watching. Imported files and import jobs stay.

post.description:
Queue folder imports for the album folders in the watch dir (or in ``path``, a
directory inside it) that are not imported or queued yet, however old: the explicit
way to import what was there before the directory was registered. Folders changed
within the settle period are left to the watcher. Returns the queued jobs.
